research_interest.title: Research Interest
paragraphs: large language models, natural language generation

projects.name: Read the Room Before Your Model Generates
description: Proposed Scenario-Actor, a framework that selects LLM decoding temperature from the communicative scenario before generation.
Designed Scenarize to map r-th layer Transformer hidden states into an interpretable scenario embedding representing conversational context.
Designed Actout, a scenario-axis readout function that maps scenario embeddings to scalar decoding temperatures.
Designed a triplet-supervised training setup to learn scenario embeddings from relative differences among communicative contexts.

projects.name: CVTime: Do LLMs Understand Chinese Vague Time Expressions in Context?
description: Introduced CVTime, the first systematic benchmark for evaluating LLM understanding of modern, cultural, and classical Chinese vague duration expressions.
Constructed 252 base items and 756 prompts covering default interpretation, contextual adjustment, fictional-rule following, source-grounded reasoning, and relative comparison.
Collected 3,024 responses from 21 annotators and preserved full response distributions to capture variation in human judgments rather than using a fixed time band.

Evaluated six LLMs with four main metrics - human-LLM agreement, ordinal distance, context-shift agreement, rule accuracy - and robustness analysis with three prompt variants and different answer orders.
Found limited human-LLM agreement and scaling effect in model size within both Qwen and Llama families, and no reliable improvement from natural context.

projects.name: Generate-then-Rerank Under Subjective Labels: Decomposing Generation and Selection Levers for Grade-Calibrated LLM Explanations
description: Developed a generate-then-rerank framework for subjective perceived-grade matching, separating generation and selection effects across Elementary, High School, and Graduate explanations.
Built a fine-tuned DistilBERT perceived-grade reranker, outperforming the strongest feature-based scorer by 7 to 13 percentage points in paired rank accuracy within each question.
Developed a diagnostic using mean pool quality and within-cell correlation to identify generation- and selection-side bottlenecks and quantify a 14.1-point oracle gap.
Conducted three human-annotation studies with over 30,000 votes, finding the best measured sampling temperature at T=1.5 and a gain of 6.2 points on deployment share from reranking.
